key_insight: A hybrid translator combines deterministic compilation for known quantum MLIR dialects with LLM agents for unseen dialects and repair, validating generated QIR through dual-backend testing.
engineering_relevance: This approach could reduce hand-written compiler work when connecting diverse quantum frameworks to QIR runtimes.
method: Use deterministic translation for Catalyst and Quake, with LLM agents handling unseen dialects and failed-output repair.
Execute source MLIR and generated QIR on independent simulators; compare output distributions using total variation distance (TVD).
Support smaller open-weight models with inline context and a guardrail assembler that rebuilds valid QIR from incomplete output.
evidence_signal: Across 41 circuits spanning three dialects and 1–100 qubits, deterministic translation was gate-exact on all 70 circuit–dialect pairs with average similarity (1−TVD) above 95%; four of six models generated valid logical-level QIR for an unseen FTQC dialect on the first iteration.
watch_item: Valid QIR and high distribution similarity do not establish full semantic equivalence or generalization beyond the tested circuits and dialects.
paper_title: Agentic MLIR-to-QIR Translation with Dual-Backend Testing: A Hybrid Deterministic and LLM Approach
